reason: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements, and no fixed release exists in any line as of 2026-10-16 - the advisory's first_patched_version is null and 1.4.0 is both the vulnerable ceiling and the newest version published to npm. It reaches this tree only through expo-updates -> @expo/code-signing-certificates (code-signing certificate parsing for OTA updates) and expo -> @expo/cli (the Expo CLI), neither of which parses attacker-supplied RSA signatures at runtime in a shipped app.
upstream: npm's suggested remediation is expo@44.0.6, a semver-major DOWNGRADE, rejected per the capped-floor doctrine. Re-check at expiry: npm view node-forge versions for a release past 1.4.0, or an expo-updates / @expo/code-signing-certificates release that drops the dependency. If neither exists, re-date with a fresh reading.

reason: zod memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections (npm audit range < 4.6.6); no patched zod 3.x exists as of 2026-10-24 - 3.25.76 is both the vulnerable ceiling of the 3.x line and its newest stable release on npm (the 3.26.0-canary prereleases above it are unpatched too). The two remaining zod 3.25.76 copies are node_modules/expo/node_modules/zod (required by @expo/cli, the Expo CLI, which imports zod only in its dev-server DevTools and MCP schemas) and node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-compiler/node_modules/zod (required by the dev-only lint plugin eslint-plugin-react-compiler and its zod-validation-error). Neither is app code: every zod import under src/ resolves to the top-level node_modules/zod, which is 4.6.7 and held there by package.json ^4.6.7. This allowance is keyed by advisory id, so it would also cover a top-level copy below 4.6.6; that package.json range is the only guard on it.
upstream: npm's suggested remediations are semver-major DOWNGRADES (expo@54.0.38 for the Expo CLI copy, eslint-plugin-react-compiler@0.0.0 for the plugin copy), rejected per the capped-floor doctrine; a floor cannot close it either, since no patched 3.x exists to cap it at. Neither upstream has moved as of 2026-10-24: all 198 @expo/cli releases that depend on zod, up to the newest (58.1.15, 2026-10-23), declare ^3.25.76, and eslint-plugin-react-compiler has had no release since 2025-08-15 (the installed 19.1.0-rc.2, its latest tag, and the newest experimental builds all declare ^3.22.4). Re-check at expiry: npm view zod versions for a stable 3.x release past 3.25.76, an @expo/cli release whose zod range is ^4, or a new eslint-plugin-react-compiler release that drops zod 3. If none exists, re-date with a fresh reading.

reason: deepmerge mergeObject() allows prototype poisoning of returned objects; GitHub rates it low (published 2026-09-18, npm audit range >=4.2.0 <=4.3.1), and no fixed release exists as of 2026-10-29 - the advisory's first_patched_version is null and 4.3.1 (published 2023-03-16) is both the vulnerable ceiling and the newest version on npm. It reaches this tree only through expo -> @expo/config (the app.json reader that the Expo CLI, prebuild config and Metro config use) and jest -> @jest/core -> jest-config (the test runner): build and test tooling, not app code - no tracked source or config file imports deepmerge, @expo/config or jest-config (app.config.ts imports only types, from expo/config). The gate reads it as high although it is low: npm audit lists @expo/cli (high through zod) and expo (high through @expo/cli) as vulnerable via @expo/config, and scripts/audit-gate.mjs gives each root advisory the severity of the package it was reached through, not its own.
upstream: npm's suggested remediations are semver-major DOWNGRADES (expo@51.0.39 for the @expo/config path, jest@25.1.0 for the jest-config path), rejected per the capped-floor doctrine; no patched deepmerge exists to put a floor on either. Re-check at expiry: npm view deepmerge versions for a release past 4.3.1, or releases of both @expo/config and jest-config that drop the dependency. If neither exists, re-date with a fresh reading.

reason: decode-uri-component denial of service through quadratic replacement of percent-encoded runs (GitHub rates it high, published 2026-10-29, vulnerable range <=0.5.0, first patched 0.5.1). The installed copy is 0.2.2 and it reaches this tree only through expo-router -> query-string@7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component. That is app runtime code: expo-router's own build code uses query-string to parse a URL's query into route params (getStateFromPath, behind its linking config for deep links). No fix is adoptable today: the patched line, 0.5.0 and 0.5.1 (published 2026-06-29 and 2026-10-23), is ESM only (type module, a default export, no CommonJS entry), while query-string 7.1.3 is CommonJS, declares ^0.2.2 and calls the result of require('decode-uri-component') as a function. Measured under Node 24.16.0 with the installed query-string pinned to 0.5.1, require() returns an object with __esModule and default and queryString.parse throws TypeError: decodeComponent is not a function (Metro and jest were not tried). npm's own remediation is a semver-major, an Expo SDK move. This allowance expires sooner than the others, 2026-11-12, because the code ships in the app.
upstream: npm's suggested remediation is expo-router@58.0.28, a semver-major that is an Expo SDK move (scripts/version-holds.json holds expo-router to 57.x), rejected per the capped-floor doctrine; an override to the patched 0.5.x is no alternative, since that line is ESM only and query-string requires it from CommonJS. Re-check at expiry: npm view expo-router versions for a 57.x release, or npm view query-string versions for a release, that takes decode-uri-component >= 0.5.1, or an override proven to work under Metro and jest. If none exists, re-date with a fresh reading.
